description: Rust port of PyDESeq2's workflow (bindings/rust, examples/deseq.rs) against PyDESeq2 0.5.2 run as a black box with RapidGLM's inference back end (rapidglm.pydeseq2.RapidGLMInference), contrast = last design column. Produced by bindings/rust/tests/compare_pydeseq2.py.
commit_note: Library code of v1.6.0-dev.2; this local 1.6.0 measurement collection was run on this commit.
timing_note: PyDESeq2 with 8 workers and Rust with 8 threads, both on CPUs 6-13 after individual quiet starts. One AMD Threadripper PRO 5965WX workstation (Zen 3). Timed work uses one thread per physical core on CPUs 6-21, with SMT siblings 30-45 idle; one thread uses CPU 6, eight use 6-13, twelve use 6-17. Drivers and untimed checks use CPUs 0-5. Exclusive Slurm allocation; schedutil governor, boost enabled and SMT enabled, unchanged. Each timed command starts after two ten-second quiet samples. More than 5% other CPU activity on selected cores or any sibling invalidates the command. Host load, other-user processes and vLLM CPU use are retained per command. From the resumed bulk stage on 2026-11-03, a user-authorized runtime service cpuset confines vLLM to CPUs 0-5,22-29,46-47; the reservation receipt records its application and restoration. Earlier accepted measurements retain their original guarded host conditions.
differences_note: The Rust workflow uses unfloored NB fits; the Python inference backend uses floored fits from 1.4.0. Low-count and boundary-fit results therefore need not match. Dispersion-trend solvers and Cook's handling also differ; these are workflow comparisons, not timings of identical fit semantics.

historical_agreement.scope: Original temporary historical tables were deleted by their comparison harness. New tables match a fresh untimed reconstruction from preserved historical binaries, and every retained historical scientific diagnostic agrees. This does not establish byte identity with the deleted original tables.

accepted_evidence: byte comparison of new accepted results against reconstruction from preserved historical binaries
user_evidence_decision.scope: Rust agreement for the resumed full 1.6.0 receipts run; no historical timings inferred from reconstruction
user_evidence_decision.statement: The user accepted exact retained historical scientific diagnostics plus byte comparison against a documented untimed reconstruction from the preserved historical binaries. The original historical raw tables are unavailable; byte identity with those deleted original tables remains unestablished.

cooks_outliers_thyroid32.note: Genes whose p-value is dropped as a Cook's outlier (missing p-value with baseMean > 0), against R DESeq2 1.48.2 run as a black box on the same design matrix. The singleton-design-cell count is a descriptive covariate, not a measured leverage-one count; singleton cells do not imply leverage one in this additive design.
